BURHAN:v3p293/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p293/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p293/r6.claim: The description of the God-fearing ends at فإذا هم مبصرون; يمدونهم in the next phrase refers to Meccan unbelievers, extended in error by their satanic brothers.
BURHAN:v3p293/r6.anchor: فهذه صفة لأتقياء المؤمنين ثم قال ﴿ يمدونهم في الغي ﴾ 8 فهذا يرجع إلى كفار مكة تمدهم

DAMGHANI:v1p299/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p299/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p299/r13.claim: A ṭāʾif can mean a whispering or prompting from Satan.
DAMGHANI:v1p299/r13.anchor: السادس الطائف الوسوسة قوله تعالى في سورة الاعراف اذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان يعني وسوسة من الشيطان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p416/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p416/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p416/r8.claim: One Qur'anic sense of ṭāʾif is satanic whispering or temptation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p416/r8.anchor: والسادس : الوسوسة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف : ﴿ إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا ﴾

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.claim: The Prophet is urged to remain steadfast against opponents’ baseless objections and is shown what can help him persevere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.anchor: At the end, the Prophet (sws) is urged to be steadfast in the wake of the nonsensical statements of his opponents and their baseless objections.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p158.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p158.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p158.claim: Although the command to forgive is singular, it addresses all Muslims through the Prophet, as the later plural address to the God-fearing confirms.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p158.anchor: Though the address in “forgive” is singular, but through the Prophet (sws) it is directed to all Muslims

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p158.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p158.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p158.claim: Remembering God gives people insight and strength, clarifying their vision so they can see reality.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p158.anchor: this remembrance will create such insight and strength in them that their vision will become absolutely clear and they will see the reality

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and al-Kisaʾi read طيف; the remaining readers read طائف.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي: " طيف " والباقون " طائف " بزنة فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda treats طيف as the verbal noun of طاف يطيف, citing a poem that uses يطيف.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r2.anchor: أحدها: أنه مصدر من طاف يطيف كباع يبيع، وأنشد أبو عبيدة:

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari derives طيف by shortening a doubled-yāʾ form, from either طاف يطيف or طاف يطوف; he compares ميت and لين, and the latter root yields طيوف with metathesis and assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه مخفف من فيعل، والأصل: طيف بتشديد الياء فحذف عين الكلمة كقولهم في ميت ميت

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa derives طيف from طوف by changing wāw to yāʾ; the author calls this remote and says examples أيد and حيل are anomalous, not analogical.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r4.anchor: الثالث: أن أصله طوف من طاف يطوف، فقلبت الواو ياء. قال أبو البقاء:

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r5.claim: The author says a quiescent wāw is no bar by itself; the issue is that the preceding consonant is not kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r5.anchor: وقوله " وإن كانت ساكنة " ليس هذا مقتضيا لمنع قلبها ياء بل كان ينبغي أن يقال:

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r6.claim: طائف is an active participle from either طاف يطوف like قائم and قائل, or طاف يطيف like بائع and مائل.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r6.anchor: وأما طائف فاسم فاعل، يحتمل أن يكون من طاف يطوف فيكون كقائم وقائل

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r7.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ is credited with treating طيف and طائف as synonymous, by deriving one as a verbal noun of the other or treating طيف as an adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r7.anchor: وقد زعم بعضهم أن طيفا وطائفا بمعنى واحد ويعزى للفراء

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r8.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r8.claim: Al-Farisi distinguishes طيف as a passing thought and طائف as a visitor or thought.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r8.anchor: وقال الفارسي: " الطيف كالخطرة، والطائف كالخاطر " ففرق بينهما

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r9.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r9.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says طيف means a demonic touch or intrusion, while طائف is what circles around a person.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r9.anchor: وقال الكسائي: " الطيف: اللمم، والطائف ما طاف حول الإنسان "

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya challenges al-Kisaʾi's distinction with al-Aʿsha's poem, where a jinn طائف visits a she-camel.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " وكيف هذا وقد قال الأعشى:

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r11.claim: The author answers Ibn Atiyya: al-Kisaʾi did not restrict his gloss to circling humans, so the poem does not refute him.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r11.anchor: ولا أدري ما تعجبه؟ وكأنه أخذ قوله " ما طاف حول الإنسان " مقيدا بالإنسان،

SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r12.speaker: أبو زيد الأنصاري
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r12.claim: Abu Zayd distinguishes طاف (came and went), أطاف (circled from all sides), and طاف الخيال (visited, with طيفا), differentiating the wāw and yāʾ roots and forms I and IV.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201/r12.anchor: وقال أبو زيد الأنصاري: " طاف: أقبل وأدبر يطوف طوفا وطوافا، وأطاف: استدار القوم

SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r1.speaker: السهيلي
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r1.claim: Al-Suhayli says no active participle is used from طاف الخيال because an imagined visitor is unreal; he construes طائف in 68:19 as a real agent, not طيف.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r1.anchor: وزعم السهيلي أنه لا يستعمل من " طاف الخيال " اسم فاعل قال:

SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r2.speaker: حسان
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r2.claim: Hassan's poem uses طيف for a jinn apparition that disturbed him.

SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r3.speaker: السدي
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi glosses طيف as madness and طائف as anger.
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: " الطيف: الجنون، والطائف: الغضب "

SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas treats طيف and طائف as equivalent, meaning نزغ (incitement or whispering).
SAMIN-DURR:7:201#2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه هما بمعنى واحد وهو النزغ

ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r4.claim: The word ṭāʾif is associated with ṭuftu aṭūfu and with a phantom that circles.
ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r4.anchor: يقال: طفت أطوف، وطاف الخيال يطيف

ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r5.claim: They reflected on the clearer proof available to them.
ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r5.anchor: أي تفكروا فيما هو أوضح لهم من الحجة

ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p396/r6.claim: Mubṣirūn means that they see with insight.

ASAD-NOTES:7:201#n165/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:201#n165/r1.speaker: Taj al-'Arus
ASAD-NOTES:7:201#n165/r1.claim: Taj al-'Arus glosses ta'if and its forms as an elusive phantom, image, or suggestion, including an obsession that obscures the mind.
ASAD-NOTES:7:201#n165/r1.anchor: "an imperceptible obsession which obscures the mind" (Taj al-'Arus).

ASAD-NOTES:7:201#n165/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:201#n165/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:201#n165/r2.claim: Because the suggestion comes from Satan, Asad considers dark suggestion an apt rendering of ta'if.
ASAD-NOTES:7:201#n165/r2.anchor: Since, in the above context, it is described as coming from Satan

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r1.claim: They read طيف without an alif; the form is a verbal noun meaning a passing touch or thought from Satan.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي: طيف* بغير ألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r2.claim: They read طائف with an alif and hamza; al-Fārisī treats it as a synonym of طيف, analogous to other nouns with source forms on فاعل.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر، وعاصم، وحمزة: طائف بألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r3.speaker: أبو زيد وأبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r3.claim: Abū Zayd says طاف طيفا of a dream apparition; Abū ʿUbayda glosses Satan’s طيف as a visitation or passing touch.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r3.anchor: أبو زيد: طاف الرجل يطوف طوفا

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r4.speaker: الأعشى
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r4.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line describes a woman as if touched by a mad spirit-visitor, illustrating the sense of طائف as an apparition.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r4.anchor: وأنشد الأعشى : وتصبح عن غب السرى وكأنما ...

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r5.claim: The verse means that a fleeting thought from Satan brushes the God-fearing; طيف is the more common verbal-noun pattern, like a passing thought, while طائف is like a visitor or mental impression.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p120/r5.anchor: فكأن المعنى: إذا مسهم وخطر لهم خطرة من الشيطان

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r1.claim: The standard reading of in waliyyi Allāh has three yāʾs: an extra yāʾ of faʿīl, the original root yāʾ, and possessive yāʾ; the first assimilates and the suffix opens at adjacent sukūns.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r1.anchor: إجماع القراء على قراءته بثلاث ياءات الأولى ياء فعيل زائدة والثانية لام الفعل أصلية والثالثة ياء الإضافة فأدغمت الزائدة في الأصلية

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r2.speaker: ابن اليزيدي عن أبيه عن أبي عمرو
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r2.claim: A report gives a doubled, open yāʾ reading of in waliyyi Allāh, deleting the middle yāʾ; the author qualifies it with if sound.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r2.anchor: إلا ما رواه ابن اليزيدي عن أبيه عن أبي عمرو ﴿ إن وليي الله ﴾ بياء مشددة مفتوحة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r3.claim: With alif, ṭāʾif is an active participle from a spirit visiting a sleeper; ṭāfa and aṭāfa are dialects, and the word means Satan's whispers and suggestions.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r3.anchor: فالحجة لمن أثبتها أنه جعله اسم الفاعل من طاف الخيال إذا طرق النائم وهما لغتان طاف طوفا وأطاف مطافا ومعنى طائف الشيطان وساوسه ولممه وختله

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r4.claim: The poet's image of a night visitor circling a woman supports the sense of ṭāʾif as a spirit that approaches during sleep.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p168/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر وتضحى على غب السرى وكأنما أطاف بها من طائف الحن أولق

QIRAAT-ER:7:201:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:201:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:201:6#1/r1.claim: Ṭayf evokes a phantom or apparition, whereas ṭāʾif retains the sense of an active circling agent.
QIRAAT-ER:7:201:6#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: ṭayf (phantom/apparition) vs ṭāʾif (circling agent)

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r12.claim: A ṭāʾif is what circles around someone; touching is bodily contact, so this expression is stronger than the lighter movement called nazgh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r12.anchor: لأن النزغ أدنى حركة والمس الإصابة والطائف ما يطوف به ويدور عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r13.claim: The Prophet's case uses in, which allows prompting to occur or not, while the pious are described with idhā, signaling certainty or a stronger likelihood of being touched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r13.anchor: حيث جاء الكلام للرسول كان الشرط بلفظ إن المحتملة للوقوع ولعدمه، وحيث كان الكلام للمتقين كان المجيء بإذا الموضوعة للتحقيق أو للترجيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p257/r14.claim: The pious remember God's commands and prohibitions after the touch has made them forget; remembrance immediately lets them see truth and right guidance, follow it, and drive Satan away.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r1.claim: The verse resumes the preceding command by showing that seeking refuge is the established practice of the Godfearing, while omitting it is the habit of the astray.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r1.anchor: إستئناف مقرر لما قبله من الأمر ببيان أن الإستعاذة سنة مسلوكة للمتقين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains طائف as a touch or whispering suggestion from Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r2.anchor: أي لمة منه كما روي عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r3.claim: The indefinite form belittles the satanic touch; calling it a circuiting visitor suggests it brushes them without affecting them, as though it circles without reaching inside.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r3.anchor: وتنويه للتحقير والمراد وسوسة ما وهو اسم فاعل من طاف بالشيء إذا دار حوله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r4.claim: The image of circling signals that Satan’s whisper touches the Godfearing without penetrating or taking effect.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r4.anchor: وجعل الوسوسة طائفا للإيذان بأنها وإن مست لا تؤثر فيهم فكأنها طافت حولهم ولم تصل إليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r5.claim: Another derivation takes طائف from a dream apparition that visits, making it a passing thought.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون من طاف طيف الخيال إذا ألم في المنام فالمراد به الخاطر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r6.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r6.claim: Several commentators understand طائف as anger.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r6.anchor: وذهب غير واحد إلى أن المراد بالطائف الغضب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, al-Kisai, and Yaqub read طيف, as a verbal noun or a lightened form from a wāw- or yāʾ-root, like هين and لين.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب ( طيف ) على أنه مصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r8.claim: Satan here means the species generally, not Iblis alone, which explains the plural pronoun used later.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r8.anchor: والمراد بالشيطان الجنس لا إبليس فقط ولذا جمع ضميره فيما سيأتي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r9.claim: Their remembrance may be of God’s commands and prohibitions, of seeking refuge in God, or of Satan’s enmity and guile.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r9.anchor: أي ما أمر الله تعالى به ونهى عنه أو الإستعاذة به تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r10.claim: Through remembrance they recognize errors and paths of right guidance, avoid disobedience, and escape what displeases God.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r10.anchor: مواقع الخطأ ومناهج الرشد فيحترزون عما يخالف أمر الله تعالى وينجون عما لا يرضيه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r11.claim: The relative phrase naturally covers everyone characterized by Godfearing, rather than a restricted group.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد من الموصول من اتصف بعنوان الصلة مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r12.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r12.claim: An unnamed critical scholar argues that if the earlier address to the Prophet is specific, the Godfearing here should be resolute messengers; if it is general, they are righteous servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r12.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : إن الخطاب في قوله سبحانه وتعالى : ( وإما ينزغنك )

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r13.claim: Alusi rejects the first conditional’s alleged necessity and says the general reading is the default in every case.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r13.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الملازمة في الشرطية الأولى في حيز المنع والعموم هو المتبادر على كل حال

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r14.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r14.claim: Some restrict those touched to non-prophets and the preceding address to Muhammad; they distinguish initial whispering نزغ from a later, established touch مس, as a mark of prophetic favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r14.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن المراد بالمتقين المنسوب إليهم المس غير الأنبياء عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r15.claim: A further explanation is that Satan expends greater effort to whisper to the perfect than to those below, hence نزغ is used earlier and مس here.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p148/r15.anchor: وقد يقال : إن إهتمام الشيطان في الوسوسة للكامل أكمل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r5.claim: Those who fear God here are the believers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr, the Basrans, and al-Kisāʾī read ṭayf, while the other readers read ṭāʾif; the two are dialectal variants meaning something that visits or touches.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأهل البصرة والكسائي: "طيف"، وقرأ الآخرون "طائف" بالمد والهمز

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r7.claim: The two readings mean something that comes upon a person.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r7.anchor: وهما لغتان كالميت والمائت، ومعناهما: الشيء يلم بك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr distinguishes ṭāʾif as something circling an object and ṭayf as a touch or whisper.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r8.anchor: فقال أبو عمرو: الطائف ما يطوف حول الشيء والطيف: اللمة والسوسة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r9.claim: Another reported distinction calls ṭāʾif Satanic whispering that circles a person and ṭayf a touch or affliction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p317/r9.anchor: وقيل: الطائف ما طاف به من وسوسة الشيطان، والطيف اللمم والمس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r1.claim: Tadhakkarū means that they recognized or came to know.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains this as someone becoming angry, remembering God, and restraining his anger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: هو الرجل يغضب الغضبة فيذكر الله تعالى فيكظم الغيظ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r3.claim: Mujāhid says it is someone intent on sin who remembers God and abandons it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو الرجل يهم بالذنب فيذكر الله فيدعه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r4.claim: By remembering and reflecting, they see where their errors lie.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r4.anchor: أي يبصرون مواقع خطاياهم بالتذكر والتفكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r5.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says that when they slip, they repent.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r6.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r6.claim: Muqātil says the God-fearing person recognizes the prompting as sin and then withdraws from disobeying God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p318/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إن المتقي إذا أصابه نزغ من الشيطان تذكر وعرف أنه معصية

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r1.claim: A ṭāʾif is a satanic touch or whisper, from ṭāfa as if circling without affecting the pious, or from the expression for a passing vision or thought.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r1.anchor: لمة منه، وهو اسم فاعل من طاف يطوف كأنها طافت بهم ودارت حولهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb read ṭayf, as a verbal noun or a shortened pronunciation like layn/hayn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب «طيف» على أنه مصدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r3.claim: Satan is generic here, which is why the pronoun referring to him is plural.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r3.anchor: والمراد بالشيطان الجنس ولذلك جمع ضميره

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r4.claim: They remember what God commanded and what He prohibited.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r4.anchor: ما أمر الله به ونهى عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r5.claim: Remembering lets them see their errors and Satan's schemes, so they guard against them and do not follow Satan in them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r5.anchor: بسبب التذكر مواقع الخطأ ومكايد الشيطان فيتحرزون عنها

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:201/r6.claim: This verse reinforces and confirms the preceding discussion.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r5.claim: The emphatic statement about the God-fearing explains the command to seek refuge and contrasts its confirmation with the earlier singular address to the Prophet.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r6.claim: Ṭāʾif can be an active participle like mayyit or māʾit, or a verbal noun; the image is Satan circling them and never leaving.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r7.claim: Satan's circuit sometimes affects them, even surrounding them from every side, and sometimes passes without effect; Satan is far from mercy and burned by the curse.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r7.anchor: فيكون قد مسهم مسا هو أكبر من النزع لكونه أطاف بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r8.claim: They make themselves remember God and whatever benefits them in both acting and refraining.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r8.anchor: كلفوا أنفسهم ذكر الله بجيع ما ينفعهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r9.claim: The nominal clause and suddenness particle portray immediate, stable insight from the light of the heart, so they do not follow Satan.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r9.anchor: أشاره إلى ذلك بالجملة الاسمية مؤكدا لسرعة البصر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p175/r10.claim: The God-fearing person desires but restrains himself and sees but refrains; one who persists with Satan becomes blind through wrongdoing, as if in darkness.

BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r2.claim: Those who have taqwa are people who protect themselves from what harms them.
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r2.anchor: {إن الذين اتقوا} أي : اتصفوا بوقاية أنفسهم عما يضرها

BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r3.claim: A satanic “touch” is the slightest prompting: a whisper or contact.
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r3.anchor: {إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان} أدنى لمة منه وهي الوسوسة والمس ،

BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r4.claim: Ṭāʾif may derive from circling around something, as a whispering temptation circles its victim.
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r4.anchor: والطائف اسم فاعل من طاف يطوف إذا دار حول الشيء كأنها تطوف بهم وتدور حولهم لتوقع بهم

BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, it may derive from a passing fancy that visits someone; al-Sihah glosses a satanic apparition or touch as a whisper, and defines a dream-image as its appearance in the imaginative faculty.
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r5.anchor: وفي "الصحاح" : طيف الخيال مجيئه في النوم وطيف من الشيطان وطائف منه لمم منه والخيال في الأصل اسم

BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r6.claim: They remember what God commanded and prohibited.
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r6.anchor: {تذكروا} أي : ما أمر به ونهى عنه.

BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r7.speaker: المولى أبو السعود
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Suud interprets their remembering as seeking refuge in God and relying on Him.
BURSEVI:v3p229#2/r7.anchor: وقال المولى أبو السعود : أي : الاستعاذة به تعالى والتوكل عليه.

BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r1.claim: Remembering makes them see errors and Satan’s snares, so they avoid them and do not follow Satan.
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r1.anchor: {فإذا هم} بسبب ذلك التذكر {مبصرون} مواقع الخطأ ومكائد الشيطان فيتحرزون عنها ولا يتبعونه فيها.

BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r6.claim: A saint asked God to show Satan’s whispering: the human form appeared like crystal with a dark nest-like mark between the shoulders; a pig-shaped Satan probed with an elephant-like trunk toward the heart, but remembrance made it retreat.
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r6.anchor: حكي أن بعض الأولياء سأل الله تعالى أن يريه كيف يأتي الشيطان ويوسوس فأراه الحق تعالى هيكل الإنسان في صورة بلور وبين كتفيه خال أسود كالعش

BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r7.claim: He says Satan whispers through a route like blood, so the Prophet cupped between his shoulders at Gabriel’s instruction; the seal there signified immunity, and the Prophet’s companion submitted, unlike Adam’s.
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r7.anchor: ولهذا السر الإلهي احتجم صلى الله عليه وسلم بين كتفيه وأمر بذلك ووصاه جبريل بذلك لتضعيف مادة الشيطان وتضييق مرصده لأنه يجري وسوسته مجرى الدم

BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r8.claim: Thoughts arise from angelic or satanic casting: a thought leading to good, safe in its outcome, stable, and turning one fully to God with pleasure in worship is angelic; the opposite is satanic.
BURSEVI:v3p229#3/r8.anchor: واعلم : أن أصل الخواطر اثنان ما يكون بإلقاء الملك وما يكون

BURSEVI:v3p230/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p230/r1.speaker: المشايخ
BURSEVI:v3p230/r1.claim: Some say Satan can disguise falsehood as truth; the Sufi masters agree that people sustained by unlawful food cannot distinguish angelic from satanic thoughts.
BURSEVI:v3p230/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم قد يلبس الشيطان ويري الباطل في صورة الحق فأجمع المشايخ على أن ما كان قوته من الحرام لا يفرق

BURSEVI:v3p230/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p230/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p230/r2.claim: Some authorities extend the inability to distinguish inspirations to anyone whose source of food is unknown.
BURSEVI:v3p230/r2.anchor: بل منهم من قال من كان قوته غير معلوم لا يفرق بينهما.

BURSEVI:v3p230/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p230/r3.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v3p230/r3.claim: The Mathnawi verses say lawful nourishment gives the soul light, strength, and desire for service and the afterlife, while illicit food breeds envy, traps, ignorance, and heedlessness.

BURSEVI:v3p230/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p230/r4.speaker: حضرة شيخنا الفريد
BURSEVI:v3p230/r4.claim: In the Lawaʾih al-barqiyya, the teacher says an angel casts truth into truthful hearts continually; a satanic touch reminds them, so they perceive it and erase it.
BURSEVI:v3p230/r4.anchor: الملك الموكل بأمر الله على قلوب أهل الحق يلقي إليهم الحق دائما فإذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان فيذكرهم بذلك الطائف الشيطاني فهم يتذكرون ويبصرون ويمحون

BURSEVI:v3p230/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p230/r5.speaker: حضرة شيخنا الفريد
BURSEVI:v3p230/r5.claim: By God’s abandonment, Satan continually casts falsehood into the breasts of false people; a touch from the Merciful makes them forget, so they neither perceive nor erase it.
BURSEVI:v3p230/r5.anchor: والشيطان المتسلط بخذلان الله على صدور أهل الباطل يلقي إليهم الباطل دائما فإذا مسهم طائف من الرحمن فينسيهم ذلك فهم لا يتذكرون ولا يبصرون ولا يمحون

BURSEVI:v3p230/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p230/r6.speaker: حضرة شيخنا الفريد
BURSEVI:v3p230/r6.claim: The Merciful affair shows truth as truth and falsehood as falsehood, while Satan shows them reversed; hence God’s servants guide and are guided, and Satan’s servants stray and mislead.
BURSEVI:v3p230/r6.anchor: فالشان الرحماني دائما إراءة الحق حقا والباطل باطلا والشان الشيطاني إراءة الحق باطلا والباطل حقا

BURSEVI:v3p230/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p230/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p230/r7.claim: The people of taqwa are people of the heart: taqwa belongs to the heart, as the Prophet indicated at his chest, and is a light that distinguishes truth from falsehood.
BURSEVI:v3p230/r7.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {إن الذين اتقوا} هم أرباب القلوب والتقوى من شان القلب كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : "التقوى ههنا"

BURSEVI:v3p230/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p230/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p230/r8.claim: A pure heart sees a satanic prompting by the light of taqwa, recognizes that it would corrupt its clarity and harden it, then remembers and avoids it.
BURSEVI:v3p230/r8.anchor: أي : إذا طاف حول القلب التقي النقي نوع طيف من عمل الشيطان يراه القلب بنور التقوى ويعرفه فيتذكر أنه يفسده ويكدر صفاءه

DURR-FULL:v3p631/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r9.claim: Mujahid identifies the God-fearing as believers.
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {إن الذين اتقوا} قال: هم المؤمنون

DURR-FULL:v3p631/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r10.claim: Mujahid glosses Satan’s touch as anger.
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان} قال: الغضب

DURR-FULL:v3p631/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise glosses the satanic touch as anger.
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الطيف: الغضب

DURR-FULL:v3p631/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r12.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak recited طائف with an alif and says one may intend an indecent act but refrain.
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r12.anchor: عن الضحاك أنه قرأ (إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان) بالألف {تذكروا} قال: هم بفاحشة

DURR-FULL:v3p631/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r13.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r13.claim: Al-Suddi explains their remembering as repenting when they stumble.
DURR-FULL:v3p631/r13.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا} يقول: إذا زلوا تابوا

DURR-FULL:v3p632/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says a servant who sins and repents draws nearer to God; repeating the sin and repenting again brings honor with Him.
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r1.anchor: من طريق وهب بن جرير عن أبيه قال: كنت جالسا عند الحسن

DURR-FULL:v3p632/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r2.claim: The Prophet compares a believer to a stalk that bends and straightens; when harvested, its owner is pleased, as the believer’s good end is praised.
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r2.anchor: ألم تسمع ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قلت: وما قال قال مثل المؤمن مثل السنبلة

DURR-FULL:v3p632/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says God does not call the believer an unbeliever after a lapse, but still calls him God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب قال: إن الله لم يسم عبده المؤمن كافرا ثم قرأ

DURR-FULL:v3p632/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r4.claim: Jabir ibn Abd Allah heard the Prophet recite طائف with an alif.
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r4.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ

DURR-FULL:v3p632/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r5.speaker: إبراهيم ويحيى بن وثاب
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r5.claim: Al-Aʿmash reports one of Ibrahim and Yahya ibn Waththab recited طائف and the other طيف, without specifying who used which form.
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r5.anchor: عن الأعمش عن إبراهيم ويحيى بن وثاب قرأ أحدهما طائف والآخر طيف

DURR-FULL:v3p632/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr recited طائف with an alif.
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أنه قرأ (إذا مسهم طائف) بالألف

DURR-FULL:v3p632/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas calls Satan’s touch a prompting; the God-fearing desist from sin, obey God, and oppose Satan.
DURR-FULL:v3p632/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: الطائف اللمة من الشيطان

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the God-fearing in this verse as believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : ان الذين اتقوا قال : هم المؤمنون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Satan's visitation as a touch or whisper from Satan.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ان الذين اتقوا اذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا والطائف اللمة من الشيطان

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd also explain 'taif' as anger.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr glosses remembering as reflecting.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r4.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن الزبير يقول : اذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تاملوا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says they may be tempted toward an indecent act but refrain from doing it.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك قوله : ان الذين اتقوا اذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان بالالام تذكروا قال : هم بفاحشة ولم يعملها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r6.speaker: العلاء بن بدر
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r6.claim: Al-Ala ibn Badr says they did commit the indecent act.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r6.anchor: وقال العلا بن بدر : قد عملها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says they remember God when they slip and then repent.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r7.anchor: عن السدى ان الذين اتقوا اذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا يقول : اذا زلوا وتابوا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that they then stop sinning, follow God's command, and disobey Satan.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : تذكروا فاذا هم مبصرون يقول : اذا هم منتهون عن المعصية

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r9.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says they see the state they are in.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1640/r9.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم في قول الله : تذكروا فاذا هم مبصرون يبصرون ما هم فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r1.claim: The sentence confirms the refuge command and explains it: when Satan's prompting is sensed, refuge is the response; its opening إن marks importance, not denial or doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r1.anchor: هذا تأكيد وتقرير للأمر بالاستعاذة من الشيطان ، فتتنزل جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r2.claim: Seeking God's protection delivers the Messenger from Satan's prompting and recalls the duty to struggle against Satan and stay alert to his schemes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r2.anchor: أولاهما أن الاستعاذة بالله منجاة للرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام من نزغ الشيطان ، والثانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r3.claim: The Messenger is commanded to resist Satan because he is pious and takes joy in following the example of earlier pious people, as in 6:90.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r3.anchor: فالرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام مأمور بمجاهدة الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r4.claim: The explanatory reason is broader than the command it explains, since remembrance covers more than seeking refuge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r4.anchor: وقد جاءت العلة هنا أعم من المعلل : لأن التذكر أعم من الاستعاذة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur conjectures that this community was specially given the practice of seeking refuge, repeatedly commanded in the Qur'an and Prophet's sayings, while earlier peoples were given remembrance, as this community was given Friday.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r5.anchor: ولعل الله ادخر خصوصية الاستعاذة لهذه الأمة ، فكثر في القرآن الأمر بالاستعاذة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r6.claim: The pious here are the messengers and the righteous among their communities, presented as exemplary models; taqwa was explained at 2:2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بهم : الرسل وصالحو أممهم ، لأنه أريد جعلهم قدوة وأسوة حسنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r7.claim: Mass literally means placing a hand on a body and is used metaphorically for affliction, including the slightest contact.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r7.anchor: و ( المس ) حقيقته وضع اليد على الجسم ، واستعير للإصابة أو لأدنى الإصابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r8.claim: A ta'if is a visitor who circles a place awaiting permission to enter; the word depicts a satanic thought at its first circulation in the mind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r8.anchor: والطائف هو الذي يمشي حول المكان ينتظر الإذن له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r9.claim: Arab custom had an arriving guest circle the household and seek leave and hospitality; Ibn Ashur cites the story of al-Nabigha with al-Nu'man as an example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p231#2/r9.anchor: وكانت عادة العرب أن القادم إلى أهل البيت ، العائذ برب البيت ، المستأنس للقرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r1.claim: The custom of circumambulating the Kaaba imitates guests approaching a household; it may explain using طائف for a hidden, fleeting visitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك طواف القادمين إلى مكة بالكعبة تشبها بالوافدين على المملوك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r2.claim: Al-A'sha's line uses طائف for a visitation by a jinn apparition, and Qur'an 68:19 calls a calamity a طائف.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r2.anchor: ألم بها من طائف الجن أولق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r3.claim: The majority read طائف with an alif and hamza; Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read طيف, without the alif and with a silent yāʾ, meaning a dream image familiar in poetry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r3.anchor: وقراءة ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب : ( طيف )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r4.claim: The conditional إذا and light-touch verb point to seeking God at the first onset of satanic thoughts, before they grow into resolve and action.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الفزع إلى الله من الشيطان ، عند ابتداء إلمام الخواطر الشيطانية بالنفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r5.claim: The definite noun may mean devils generically or refer to Iblis, since his army's whispering is attributed to his command and authority.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يكون تعريف الجنس : أي من الشياطين ويجوز أن يكون تعريف العهد والمراد به إبليس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r6.claim: Remembering is bringing prior knowledge to mind, especially God's commands; it can include recalling refuge if that practice was prescribed to earlier peoples and is prescribed to this community.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r7.claim: Following the pious includes recollecting and carrying out all commanded duties, not just seeking refuge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r7.anchor: فالاقتداء بالذين اتقوا يعم سائر أحوال التذكر للمأمورات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r8.claim: The result-fāʾ and sudden إذا stress immediate insight: once firm remembrance occurs, they quickly see the truth, leave the satanic thought, and act by what they remembered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p232/r8.anchor: وأكد معنى ( فاء ) التعقيب ب ( إذا ) الفجائية الدالة على حصول مضمون جملتها دفعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r1.claim: Taqwa here includes avoiding both shirk and sins, since the people are praised; it cannot mean avoiding shirk alone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r1.anchor: اتقوا هنا عامة في اتقاء الشرك واتقاء المعاصي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r2.claim: Even the pious can be touched by Satan, since only the prophets are infallible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r2.anchor: إذ ليست العصمة إلا للأنبياء عليهم السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r3.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r3.claim: Nafiʿ, ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, and Hamza read ṭāʾif; Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and al-Kisaʾi read ṭayf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة «طائف» ، وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي «طيف»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr also reads ṭayf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير «طيف» ، واللفظة إما من طاف يطوف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r5.claim: The word may derive from ṭāfa-yatūfu or ṭāfa-yaṭīfu; ṭāʾif is an active participle, and ṭayf has active-participle or shortened formations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r5.anchor: ف «طائف» اسم فاعل كقائل من قال يقول وكبائع من باع يبيع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r6.claim: Abu ʿUbayda's verse attests Arab use of the form yaṭīf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r6.anchor:
أنشد أبو عبيدة في ذلك:
أنى الم بك الخيال يطيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r7.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi favors derivation from ṭāfa-yaṭīfu, with ṭāʾif meaning a thought and ṭayf a passing notion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r7.anchor: وإلى هذا مال أبو علي الفارسي وجعل الطائف كالخاطر والطيف كالخطرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r8.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r8.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says tayf is a touch and taʾif circles a person; Ibn ʿAtiyya challenges this using al-Aʿsha's description of a jinn seizure as a taʾif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r8.anchor: وقال الكسائي: الطيف اللمم والطائف ما طاف حول الإنسان.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya challenges al-Kisaʾi's distinction by citing al-Aʿsha's line about a taʾif of the jinn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r9.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وكيف هذا وقد قال الأعشى: [الطويل]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r10.claim: The verse describes an episode of anger accompanied by Satan's making something improper seem attractive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r10.anchor: ومعنى الآية: إذا مسهم غضب وزين الشيطان معه ما لا ينبغي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r11.claim: Remembering refers back to the commanded seeking of refuge and to God's commands and prohibitions concerning the temptation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r11.anchor: وقوله تذكروا إشارة إلى الاستعاذة المأمور بها قبل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r12.speaker: ابن الزبير وأبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r12.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads taʾammalū; Ubayy's codex has a reordered phrase with taʾammalū.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير «من الشيطان تأملوا فإذا هم» ، وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب «إذا طاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r13.claim: The Prophet calls anger a troop of the jinn, marked by red eyes and swollen veins, and advises seeking refuge when it occurs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r13.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الغضب جند من جند الجن،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r14.claim: Mubṣirūn means that they discern the truth and turn toward it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p491#3/r14.anchor: وقوله مبصرون من البصيرة أي فإذا هم قد تبينوا الحق ومالوا إليه.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī read طيف without alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي طيف بغير ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥamza read طائف with a long alif and hamza.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة طائف بألف ممدودا مهموزا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير والجحدري والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr, al-Jaḥdarī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read طيف with doubled yāʾ and no alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن جبير والجحدري والضحاك طيف بتشديد الياء من غير ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r4.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says طائف and طيف have the same sense, like an apparition or something that visits; al-Akhfash says طيف is more common in Arabic and cites a line about a light phantom.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r4.anchor: وهما ما كان كالخيال والشيء يلم بك حكي عن الفراء وقال الأخفش الطيف أكثر في كلام العرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r5.claim: A distinction attributed to Abū ʿAmr makes طائف something circling around an object, while طيف is a touch, Satanic whisper, or passing thought.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r5.anchor: أن الطائف ما يطوف حول الشيء والطيف اللمة والوسوسة والخطرة حكي عن أبي عمرو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to call طائف a Satanic touch and طيف anger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال الطائف اللمة من الشيطان والطيف الغضب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī derives طائف as the agent form from طيف and says linguists use طيف for a Satanic lapse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن الانباري الطائف الفاعل من الطيف والطيف عند أهل اللغة اللمم من الشيطان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p309#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid identifies the Satanic طائف as anger.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the God-fearing remember God when they are about to sin, then leave the sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r1.anchor: تذكروا الله إذا هموا بالمعاصي فتركوها قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains that they reflect on the proof God has made clear to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r2.anchor: تفكروا فيما أوضح الله لهم من الحجة قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r3.claim: They recall God’s anger when Satan emboldens them toward the unlawful, restrain themselves, and by reflection see where error lies.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p310/r3.anchor: تذكروا غضب الله والمعنى إذا جرأهم الشيطان على مالا يحل تذكروا غضب الله فأمسكوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r1.claim: The verse describes the God-fearing as obedient to commands and abstinent from prohibitions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن المتقين من عباده الذين أطاعوه فيما أمر، وتركوا ما عنه زجر، أنهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r2.claim: Two famous readings are taʾif and ṭaif; some consider them synonymous, while others distinguish them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r2.anchor: وهما قراءتان مشهورتان، فقيل: بمعنى واحد. وقيل: بينهما فرق،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r3.speaker: مفسرون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r3.claim: Reported explanations of the satanic touch include anger, seizure or a similar affliction, an intention to sin, and committing a sin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r3.anchor: ومنهم من فسر ذلك بالغضب، ومنهم من فسره بمس الشيطان بالصرع ونحوه، ومنهم من فسره بالهم بالذنب،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r4.claim: They remember God’s punishment and great reward, His promise and threat, then repent, turn back quickly, and seek refuge in Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r4.anchor: وقوله: {تذكروا} أي: عقاب الله وجزيل ثوابه، ووعده ووعيده، فتابوا وأنابوا، واستعاذوا بالله ورجعوا إليه من قريب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r5.claim: They become clear-sighted, upright, and recovered from the state they were in.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r5.anchor: قد استقاموا وصحوا مما كانوا فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a woman with seizures asking the Prophet for healing; she chose patience and Paradise, asking him to pray that she not become exposed, and he prayed for her. Al-Hakim graded the report sound by Muslim’s criteria, though neither included it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r6.anchor: عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: جاءت امرأة إلى النبي (2) صلى الله عليه وسلم وبها طيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r7.speaker: ابن عساكر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r7.claim: Ibn Asakir recounts that a young worshipper remembered this verse while tempted into adultery, collapsed and died; Umar prayed at his grave, cited 55:46, and heard the youth say God gave him the two gardens twice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p534/r7.anchor: وقد ذكر الحافظ ابن عساكر في ترجمة "عمرو بن جامع" من تاريخه: أن شابا كان يتعبد في المسجد،

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and al-Kisai read طيف without an alif; the Nakhai and al-Aswad ibn Yazid also read it so.
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي: طيف بغير ألف

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r2.claim: The remaining readers use طائف with an alif.

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r3.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj cites طفت عليه and طاف الخيال; الطائف is like a passing thought or occurrence.
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: طفت عليه أطوف، وطاف الخيال يطيف

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r4.claim: One view treats الطيف and الطائف as synonyms, like الميت and المائت; another distinguishes them.
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r4.anchor: واختلفوا فقيل: الطيف والطائف واحد، كالميت والمائت

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r11.claim: مس means touching by hand; related uses describe one afflicted by touch and water reached by hands.
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r11.anchor: المس: مس الشيء بيدك، يقال: مسسته أمسه

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r12.claim: طيف derives from the wāw-root طاف; a doubled form may also have been lightened, like كيد and ميت.
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r12.anchor: الطيف أصله الواو، ويقال: طاف يطوف طوفا وطوافا

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r13.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses يطيف as evidence for the word's form.
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r13.anchor: قال الشاعر: أنى ألم بك الخيال يطيف

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r14.speaker: ابن فارس وابن عرفة
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r14.claim: Ibn Faris and Ibn Arafa define الطيف and الطائف alike as a jinn or apparition hovering around a person.
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r14.anchor: قال ابن فارس وابن عرفة: الطيف والطائف

JISHUMI:v4p2825/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r15.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r15.claim: Abu Amr and Abu Ubayd distinguish them: الطائف is Satan's whispering, while الطيف is madness.
JISHUMI:v4p2825/r15.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو وأبو عبيد: الطائف

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r1.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r1.claim: Nafiʿ, ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, and Hamza read ṭāʾif.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة { طآئف }

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r3.claim: One view treats the two readings as equivalent in meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r3.anchor: واختلف في هاتين القراءتين على قولين : أحدهما : أن معناهما واحد وإن اختلف اللفظان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r4.claim: One gloss takes ṭayf as a fleeting visitation, like an apparition that brushes a person.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r4.anchor: أن الطيف اللمم كالخيال يلم بالإنسان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r5.claim: Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ glosses it as whispering.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r5.anchor: والثاني : أنه الوسوسة , قاله أبو عمرو بن العلاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses it as fear or alarm.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r7.anchor: والرابع , أنه الفزع , قاله سعيد بن جبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r8.claim: A second view distinguishes the readings' meanings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r8.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن معنى الطيف والطائف مختلفان , فالطيف اللمم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r9.claim: On the distinction view, ṭayf is a fleeting visitation, while ṭāʾif is anything that circles around a person.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r9.anchor: فالطيف اللمم , والطائف كل شيء طاف بالإنسان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r10.claim: One explanation is that they recognize the danger and then desist.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r10.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : علموا فإذا هم منتهون

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p289/r11.claim: A second explanation is that they reflect and then become guided.

MUJAHID:v1p253#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p253#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p253#2/r1.claim: The satanic impulse that touches them is anger.
MUJAHID:v1p253#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان ﴾ قال هو الغضب

MUQATIL:7:201-203/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:201-203/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:201-203/r1.claim: Those who guard themselves are people who avoid polytheism.
MUQATIL:7:201-203/r1.anchor: { إن الذين اتقوا } الشرك، { إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا فإذا هم مبصرون } [آية:201]

MUQATIL:7:201-203/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:201-203/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:201-203/r2.claim: When Satan incites them, the God-fearing recognize the sin and recoil from it out of fear of God.
MUQATIL:7:201-203/r2.anchor: يقول: إن المتقين إذا أصابهم نزغ من الشيطان، تذكروا وعرفوا أنها معصية، ففزعوا منها من مخافة الله.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r1.speaker: مكى وبصرى
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r1.claim: Meccan and Basran readers have ṭayf in place of ṭāʾif.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r1.anchor: إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان ﴾ طيف مكى وبصرى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr says the two readings mean the same thing; the word denotes a satanic whisper.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r2.anchor: وعن أبى عمرو هما واحد وهى الوسوسة وهذا تأكيد لما تقدم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r3.claim: The verse reinforces the preceding command to seek refuge in God when Satan provokes.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r3.anchor: وهذا تأكيد لما تقدم من وجوب الاستعاذة بالله عند نزغ الشيطان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r4.claim: Pious people recall God's commands and prohibitions when touched even slightly by whispering, then see clearly and repel it by fleeing to God, gaining insight through Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p52#6/r4.anchor: إذا أصابهم ادنى نزغ من الشيطان وإلمام بوسوسته

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r1.claim: The God-fearing are those who avoid idolatry and sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إن الذين اتقوا } يريد الشرك والمعاصي.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r2.speaker: أهل البصرة وأهل مكة وأهل المدينة وأهل الكوفة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r2.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل البصرة وأهل مكة وقراءة أهل المدينة وأهل الكوفة «طائف».

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports طيف with a doubled yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r3.anchor: وروي عن سعيد بن جبير «طيف» بتشديد الياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r4.claim: Al-Nahhas says the ordinary verbal noun is lightened طيف from طاف يطيف.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r4.anchor: قال النحاس: كلام العرب في مثل هذا «طيف» بالتخفيف على أنه مصدر من طاف يطيف.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r5.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi treats the form as lightened, like the variants ميت and ميت.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r5.anchor: قال الكسائي: هو مخفف من «طيف» مثل ميت وميت.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r6.speaker: النحاس وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r6.claim: Al-Nahhas says the word can mean an image imagined in the mind or seen in sleep; Abu Hatim cites al-Asmaʿi's objection to its pattern, which al-Nahhas answers by treating it as طائف.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r6.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: سألت الأصمعي عن طيف فقال: ليس في المصادر فيعل. قال النحاس: ليس هو بمصدر، ولكن يكون بمعنى طائف

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r7.speaker: السهيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r7.claim: Al-Suhayli distinguishes an unreal mental image طيف from Satan himself as طائف; the real visitor in 68:19 is said to be Gabriel.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r7.anchor: وقيل: الطيف والطائف معنيان مختلفان. فالأول التخيل. والثاني الشيطان نفسه. فالأول مصدر طاف الخيال يطوف طيفا ولم يقولوا من هذا طائف في اسم الفاعل. قال السهيلي:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r8.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj distinguishes طفت عليهم أطوف from طاف الخيال يطيف.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج: طفت عليهم أطوف، وطاف الخيال يطيف.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r9.speaker: حسان
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r9.claim: Hassan's line uses لطيف for a phantom that keeps him awake at night.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r9.anchor:
وقال حسان:
فدع هذا ولكن من لطيف

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r10.claim: Mujahid says ṭayf means anger; madness, anger, and whispering are called ṭayf because a satanic touch resembles an imagined visit.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r10.anchor: مجاهد: الطيف الغضب. ويسمى الجنون والغضب والوسوسة طيفا لأنه لمة من الشيطان

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r11.anchor: أي منتهون. وقيل: فإذا هم على بصيرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والنحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r12.claim: Saʿid reads تذكروا with doubled dhāl, but al-Nahhas says the reading has no basis in Arabic.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r12.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير: «تذكروا» بتشديد الذال. ولا وجه له في العربية ذكره النحاس.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r13.speaker: عصام بن المصطلق
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r13.claim: Asim recounts insulting Hasan ibn Ali from hostility; Hasan replies gently with Quran, offers help, and Asim leaves remorseful and loving him and his father.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:201-202/r13.anchor: قال عصام بن المصطلق: دخلت المدينة فرأيت الحسن بن علي عليهما السلام، فأعجبني سمته

QASHANI:7:201-205/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:201-205/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:201-205/r1.claim: The pious avoid shirk; Satan’s touch is attributing an act to someone besides God, and recollection of tawhid makes them see God’s agency alone.
QASHANI:7:201-205/r1.anchor: الشرك { إذا مسهم طائف } لمسة { من الشيطان } بنسبة الفعل إلى الغير

RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r1.claim: Remembering God's great blessings and severe punishment turns a person from natural impulse toward obedience to divine law.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r1.anchor: أن يتذكر المرء عظيم نعم الله عليه وشديد عقابه فيدعوه كل واحد من هذين الأمرين

RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r2.claim: Though the address is to the Messenger, it teaches all accountable people: seeking refuge this way protects against Satan's whispering.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r2.anchor: هذا الخطاب وإن خص الله به الرسول إلا أنه تأديب عام لجميع المكلفين

RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r3.claim: The command to seek refuge before Qurʾānic recitation shows refuge counters Satan's incitement and should be practiced often.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r3.anchor: ولذلك قال تعالى : { فإذا قرأت القرءان فاستعذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم * إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين ءامنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون }

RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r4.claim: Spoken refuge only benefits when the heart understands its meaning; bare speech without inward knowledge has no effect.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80/r4.anchor: فكأنه تعالى قال : اذكر لفظ الاستعاذة بلسانك فإني سميع واستحضر معاني الاستعاذة بعقلك وقلبك فإني عليم

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r1.claim: The Prophet may receive an initial satanic nudge; the pious may be touched by a ṭāʾif, which al-Rāzī says is more forceful.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r1.anchor: لأن الرسول لا يحصل له من الشيطان إلا النزغ الذي هو كالابتداء في الوسوسة ، وجوز في المتقين ما يزيد عليه

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī read ṭayf without alif; the others read ṭāʾif with alif.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي { * طيف } بغير ألف ، والباقون { مسهم طئف } بالألف

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r3.speaker: أبو زيد
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r3.claim: Abū Zayd relates ṭayf to movement back and forth and aṭāfa to circling people from all sides; a dream apparition also visits as ṭayf.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو زيد يقال : طاف يطوف طوفا وطوافا إذا أقبل وأدبر . وأطاف يطيف إطافة

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says ṭayf may derive from ṭayyif, with one yāʾ dropped for ease, like hayyin and mayyit.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : وجائز أن يكون طيف أصله طيف . إلا أنهم استثقلوا التشديد ، فحذفوا إحدى الياءين

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's doubled reading of the word for being touched supports Ibn al-Anbārī's derivation.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r5.anchor: ويشهد لصحة قول ابن الأنباري قراءة سعيد بن جبير { إذا مسهم } بالتشديد

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r6.claim: Madness, anger, and whispering are called ṭayf because each is a passing satanic touch resembling a dream apparition.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r6.anchor: ثم سمى الجنون والغضب والوسوسة طيفا ، لأنه لمة من لمة الشيطان تشبه لمة الخيال .

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r7.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r7.claim: Al-Azharī says ṭayf means madness in Arabic; anger is also called ṭayf because an angry person resembles someone insane.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r7.anchor: قال الأزهري : الطيف في كلام العرب الجنون ، ثم قيل للغضب طيف ، لأن الغضبان يشبه المجنون .

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r8.claim: Ṭāʾif may have the same sense as ṭayf, like verbal nouns formed on the fāʿil or fāʿila pattern.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r8.anchor: وأما الطائف فيجوز أن يكون بمعنى الطيف ، مثل العافية والعاقبة

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats ṭāʾif and ṭayf alike as an apparition; another view distinguishes a passing thought from a suggestion.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r9.anchor: قال الفراء في هذه الآية : الطائف والطيف سواء ، وهو ما كان كالخيال الذي يلم بالإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r10.claim: Another reported distinction makes ṭayf a passing thought and ṭāʾif a thought or suggestion.
RAZI-FULL:v15p80#2/r10.anchor: ومنهم من قال : الطيف كالخطرة والطائف كالخاطر

RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r1.claim: Anger arises when one judges another's act reprehensible, believes oneself capable of retaliation, and believes the other unable to defend themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r1.anchor: اعلم أن الغضب إنما يهيج بالإنسان إذا استقبح من المغضوب عليه عملا من الأعمال

RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r2.claim: Awareness of the unseen dissolves the first judgment: God created the offender's decisive motive, which God's foreknowledge made unavoidable.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r2.anchor: فإذا انكشف له أنه إنما أقدم على ذلك العمل ، لأنه تعالى خلق فيه داعية جازمة راسخة

RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r3.claim: A saying attributed to the Prophet states that whoever knows God's secret in decree finds afflictions easy; al-Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r3.anchor: وإليه الإشارة بقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( من عرف سر الله في القدر هانت عليه المصائب )

RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r4.claim: The second and third judgments are false: God could punish the angry person but has spared him, and he is as powerless before God as his target is before him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r4.anchor: أنه يعتقد أنه كم أساء في العمل ، والله كان قادرا عليه ، وهو كان أسيرا في قبضة قدرة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r5.claim: Remembering God's command to restrain anger and stop harming or alienating others undermines the urge to retaliate.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r5.anchor: أن يتذكر الغضبان ما أمره الله به من ترك إمضاء الغضب والرجوع إلى ترك الإيذاء والإيحاش .

RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r6.claim: Revenge makes a person like harmful beasts and deadly snakes, while forgiveness aligns the person with eminent prophets and saints.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r6.anchor: ورابعها : أن يتذكر أنه إذا أمضى الغضب وانتقم كان شريكا للسباع المؤذية والحياة القاتلة / وإن ترك الانتقام واختار العفو

RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r7.claim: The apparent target may later become powerful and retaliate harshly; forgiving instead becomes an act of kindness.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r7.anchor: أنه ربما انقلب ذلك الضعيف قويا قادرا عليه ، فحينئذ ينتقم منه على أسوأ الوجوه

RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r8.claim: These considerations weaken the three angry assumptions; once recalled, Satan's touch vanishes and insight frees the person from whispering.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81/r8.anchor: وبالجملة فالمراد من قوله تعالى : { اتقوا إذا مسهم طئف من الشيطان تذكروا } ما ذكرناه من الاعتقادات الثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v15p81#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p81#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p81#2/r1.claim: In 'fa-idhā hum mubṣirūn,' idhā marks sudden discovery, while idhā in 'when something touches them' introduces a condition that calls for a consequence.
RAZI-FULL:v15p81#2/r1.anchor: معنى { إذا } ههنا للمفاجأة ، كقولك خرجت فإذا زيد

STUDYQURAN:7:201/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r1.claim: Ṭāʾif denotes a visitation from Satan, perhaps experienced as a dream or apparition, and so describes temptation.
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r1.anchor: which is the lexical meaning of ṭāʾif (Z), translated here as “visitation.”

STUDYQURAN:7:201/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r2.claim: Some take Satan's visitation as an impulse toward anger.
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r2.anchor: Some consider a visitation from Satan to refer here to the impulse toward anger (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:7:201/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r3.claim: Others take it as any Satanic whispering that tempts a person toward moral or intellectual lapse.
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r3.anchor: or to any Satanic insinuation (“whispering”; see 114:4c) that tempts one toward a moral or intellectual lapse

STUDYQURAN:7:201/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r4.claim: The reverent remember God, especially His commands and threat of punishment, and return to obedience.
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r4.anchor: they remember God, and in particular they remember the commands of God and the threat of His punishment—and so return to obedience

STUDYQURAN:7:201/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r5.claim: Tadhakkarū can mean to reflect or take heed as well as to remember.
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r5.anchor: which can also mean to“reflect” or “take heed.”

STUDYQURAN:7:201/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r6.claim: After remembering, the reverent regain sound judgment and guidance and return to what is right and commanded by God.
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r6.anchor: they are restored to sound judgment and guidance (Ṭs) and return to what is right and what God has commanded

STUDYQURAN:7:201/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r7.speaker: al-Zamakhsharī
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says that remembering God whenever tempted is the reverent person's regular habit.
STUDYQURAN:7:201/r7.anchor: According to al-Zamakhsharī“remembering” God in this way whenever one is tempted is the regular habit of the reverent.

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r1.claim: The God-fearing fulfill obligations and avoid sins; when satanic prompting touches them, they recall God's reward and punishment, see truth, obey God, and leave Satan's way.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r1.anchor: تذكروا عقاب الله وثوابه ووعده ووعيده، وأبصروا الحق فعملوا به، وانتهوا

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r2.speaker: قراء أهل المدينة والكوفة
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r2.claim: Most Medinan and Kufan reciters read ṭāʾif on the fāʿil pattern.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r2.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء أهل المدينة والكوفة: {طائف} [الأعراف: 201] على مثال فاعل

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r3.speaker: بعض المكيين والبصريين والكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r3.claim: Some Meccan, Basran, and Kufan reciters read ṭayf instead.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r3.anchor: وقرأه بعض المكيين والبصريين والكوفيين: (طيف من الشيطان)

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r4.speaker: بعض البصريين
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r4.claim: Some Basrans say ṭāʾif and ṭayf have the same sense: an apparition or something that alights; ṭayf may be shortened like mayyit/mayt.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r4.anchor: قال بعض البصريين: الطائف والطيف سواء، وهو ما كان كالخيال والشيء يلم بك

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r5.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r5.claim: Some Kufans distinguish ṭāʾif as satanic whispering circling a person and ṭayf as a light touch or intrusion.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r5.anchor: قال بعض الكوفيين: الطائف: ما طاف بك من وسوسة الشيطان، وأما الطيف: فإنما هو من اللمم والمس

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r6.speaker: آخر من الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r6.claim: Another Kufan says ṭayf means an intrusion, while ṭāʾif means anything that circles a person.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r6.anchor: وقال آخر منهم: الطيف: اللمم، والطائف: كل شيء طاف بالإنسان

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr b. al-ʿAlāʾ says ṭayf means satanic whispering.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r7.anchor: وذكر عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أنه كان يقول: الطيف: الوسوسة

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers ṭāʾif because exegetes gloss it as anger or a lapse caused by what circles a person; this fits Satan's circling to mislead or whisper, whereas ṭayf denotes an apparition.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r8.anchor: وأولى القراءتين في ذلك عندي بالصواب قراءة من قرأ: {طائف من الشيطان} [الأعراف: 201] لأن أهل التأويل تأولوا ذلك بمعنى الغضب

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r9.claim: He treats ṭayf as an apparition from ṭāfa yaṭūfu and contrasts ṭāʾif from ṭāfa yaṭīfu.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r9.anchor: وأما الطيف فإنما هو الخيال، وهو مصدر من طاف يطيف

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r10.speaker: بعض البصريين وبعض الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r10.claim: Some Basrans and Kufans cite Arab usage of ṭāfa yaṭīfu and a verse using yaṭīfu as evidence for that verb.
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r10.anchor: وحكى البصريون وبعض الكوفيين سماعا من العرب: طاف يطيف، وطفت أطيف

TAB-FULL:v10p646/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p646/r11.claim: He cites a poetic line about a phantom visiting and circling someone as evidence for the verb form.

TAB-FULL:v10p649/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r1.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r1.claim: Saʿīd glosses Satan's ṭāʾif as anger.
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r1.anchor: عن أشعث، عن جعفر، عن سعيد: " {إذا مسهم طائف} [الأعراف: 201] قال: الطيف: الغضب

TAB-FULL:v10p649/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
