TAB-FULL:v10p649/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r2.claim: Mujāhid repeatedly explains the satanic touch or ṭāʾif as anger.
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: (إذا مسهم طيف من الشيطان) قال: هو الغضب

TAB-FULL:v10p649/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls the ṭāʾif a satanic lamma, a touch or intrusion.
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا} [الأعراف: 201] الطائف: اللمة

TAB-FULL:v10p649/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r4.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās glosses Satan's influence as a prompting or incitement.
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان} [الأعراف: 201] يقول: نزغ من الشيطان

TAB-FULL:v10p649/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says that when they slip, they repent.
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r5.anchor: عن السدي: " {إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا} [الأعراف: 201] يقول: إذا زلوا تابوا

TAB-FULL:v10p649/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī sees anger and satanic intrusion as related misguidance, so the verse broadly covers any satanic prompting that makes the God-fearing remember God's command and desist.
TAB-FULL:v10p649/r6.anchor: وهذان التأويلان متقاربا المعنى؛ لأن الغضب من استزلال الشيطان، واللمة من الخطيئة أيضا منه

TAB-FULL:v10p650/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p650/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p650/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that they desist from sin, obey God's command, and disobey Satan.
TAB-FULL:v10p650/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {فإذا هم مبصرون} [الأعراف: 201] يقول: إذا هم منتهون عن المعصية، آخذون بأمر الله، عاصون للشيطان

SULAMI:v1p252#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p252#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p252#2/r1.claim: The pious are those whose innermost selves roam in intimacy and nearness while they guard themselves from trials and the devil's attacks; when touched by the devil, they remember.
SULAMI:v1p252#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : من جال سره في ميادين الأنس والقربة ، وحجز نفسه عن طوارق الفتنة وطوائف الشيطان

SULAMI:v1p252#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p252#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p252#2/r2.claim: People contemplating inner secrets include those with an inner warning that prompts remembrance and those with an inner restraint, linked to the command to restrain the self from desire.
SULAMI:v1p252#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : الناس في مطالعة الأسرار على وجوه ثلاثة : منهم من له من سره مطالع يطالعه فذلك قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r2.claim: Verse 7:201 explains the preceding command to seek refuge when Satan incites.
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r2.anchor: نحو تعليل للأمر في الآية السابقة

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r3.claim: The satanic visitation may be Satan circling the heart to cast a whisper, or the whisper itself circling until it enters and settles; the senses converge.
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r3.anchor: الذي يطوف حول القلب ليلقي إليه الوسوسة أو وسوسته التي تطوف حول القلب لتقع فيه وتستقر عليه

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r4.claim: Min is explanatory on the first interpretation of the visitation and originative on the second.

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r5.claim: Remembrance is reflection that guides a person to a conclusion previously overlooked or unknown.
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r5.anchor: والتذكر تفكر من الانسان في أمور لتهديه إلى نتيجة مغفول عنها أو مجهولة قبله

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r6.claim: The God-fearing remember that God is their Lord who owns and nurtures them; entrusting their affairs to Him defeats Satan’s plot and removes heedlessness.
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r6.anchor: تذكروا أن الله هو ربهم الذي يملكهم ويربيهم يرجع إليه أمرهم

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r7.claim: Their restored insight means the veil of heedlessness no longer covers their sight.
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r7.anchor: ورفع عنهم حجاب الغفلة فإذا هم مبصرون غير مضروب على أبصارهم بحجاب الغفلة

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r8.claim: The verse parallels the assurance that Satan has no authority over believers who rely on God.
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r8.anchor: في معنى قوله إنه ليس له سلطان على الذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

TABATABAI:7:201-204/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r9.claim: Seeking refuge is remembrance because it recognizes God as the sole support against the attacking enemy; it is also reliance on God.
TABATABAI:7:201-204/r9.anchor: الاستعاذة بالله نوع من التذكر لأنها مبنية على أن الله سبحانه وهو ربه هو الركن الوحيد

TABRISI:7:201-203/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203/r1.claim: The Basrans, Ibn Kathīr, and al-Kisāʾī read ṭayf without alif, as do al-Nakhaʿī and al-Aswad b. Zayd; the others read ṭāʾif with alif.
TABRISI:7:201-203/r1.anchor: القراءة: قرأ أهل البصرة وابن كثير والكسائي طيف بغير ألف

TABRISI:7:201-203/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203/r3.claim: Ṭayf is the verbal noun for a dream apparition visiting someone, hence a passing thought; ṭāʾif has the same sense, like khāṭir, though ṭayf is more common.
TABRISI:7:201-203/r3.anchor: الطيف مصدر طاف الخيال يطيف طيفا إذا ألم به في المنام

TABRISI:7:201-203/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203/r4.claim: The line about ṭayf al-khayāl witnesses a phantom; al-Aʿshā’s verse uses ṭāʾif for a jinn visitation.
TABRISI:7:201-203/r4.anchor: وقال الأعشى: وتصبح عن غب السرى وكأنما ألم بها من طائف الجن أولق

TABRISI:7:201-203/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203/r8.claim: Al-mamsūs can mean someone touched by jinn; of water, it means water touched by hands.
TABRISI:7:201-203/r8.anchor: الممسوس الذي به مس جن والممسوس من المياه ما نالته الأيدي

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r3.claim: The first idh is temporal and takes a response like a conditional; the second is locative and marks sudden appearance.
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r3.anchor: الإعراب: إذا الأولى ظرف زمان ويكون لها جواب بمنزلة الجزاء

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r4.claim: The pious are those who avoid disobedience to God.
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r4.anchor: { إن الذين اتقوا } الله باجتناب معاصيه

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī say Satan whispers and tempts them toward sin; they recall its punishment and desist.
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r5.anchor: قيل معناه إذا وسوس إليهم الشيطان وأغراهم بمعصيته

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains this as Satan circling them with whispers.
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: يعني إذا طاف عليهم الشيطان بوساوسه

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r7.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr and Mujāhid say it describes someone who gets angry, remembers God, and restrains his anger.
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو الرجل الذي يغضب الغضبة فيتذكر فيكظم غيظه

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid also says it is someone intending a sin who remembers God and abandons it.
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r8.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا أنه قال هو الرجل يهم بالذنب

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r9.claim: Some say ṭāʾif means anger and ṭayf means madness; another view treats them as synonymous.

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r10.claim: They then see the right path clearly.

TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r21.claim: The excerpt begins an anonymous coherence note saying this verse connects to an earlier statement, but cuts off before identifying it.
TABRISI:7:201-203#2/r21.anchor: النظم: قيل إن هذه الآية اتصلت بقوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the God-fearing as believers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says they avoided unbelief, associating partners with God, and grave indecencies.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ({إن الذين اتقوا} الكفر والشرك والفواحش)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r3.claim: A variant reading substitutes طيف for طائف.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r3.anchor: وقرئ (¬6) {طيف}، اختلفوا في الطيف، فقيل: إنه مصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r4.claim: Abu Zayd explains طاف as coming and going, أطاف as circling people, and طيف as a dream apparition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو زيد: (طاف يطوف طوفا وطوافا، إذا أقبل وأدبر، وأطاف يطيف إطافة إذا جعل يستدير بالقوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives a similar explanation; a line describes an apparition coming near.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r5.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الزجاج (¬2)، وأنشدوا (¬3): أنى ألم بك الخيال يطيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari allows an original doubled yāʾ, with one yāʾ dropped as too heavy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (وجائز أن يكون الطيف أصله طيف إلا أنهم أستثقلوا التشديد فحذفوا إحدى اليائين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r7.claim: Abu Bakr treats the form on the pattern of هين and ميت.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r7.anchor: فعلى القول الأول هو مصدر، و (¬6) على ما قاله أبو بكر من باب هين وهين، وميت وميت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r8.claim: The doubled طيف reading transmitted from Said ibn Jubayr witnesses to the original form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r8.anchor: ويشهد بصحة قول أبي بكر قراءة سعيد بن # جبير (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r9.claim: Madness, anger, and whispering are called tayf because each is a touch from Satan resembling an apparition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r9.anchor: ثم يسمى الجنون والغضب والوسوسة طيفا لأنه لمة من الشيطان (¬3) يشبه بلمة الخيال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r10.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r10.claim: Al-Azhari says tayf means madness in Arabic, citing Abu Ubayd's transmission from al-Ahmar and a Hudhali poet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r10.anchor: قال الأزهري: (الطيف في كلام العرب الجنون، رواه أبو عبيد عن الأحمر (¬4). وقال الهذلي (¬5): وإذا بها وأبيك طيف جنون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r11.claim: Anger is called tayf because the mind of the person it provokes departs, making him like someone bereft of reason.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r11.anchor: وقيل للغضب: طيف لأن عقل من استفزه يعزب حتى يصير في صورة المجنون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r12.claim: Ṭāʾif may mean the same as ṭayf, as verbal nouns sometimes take فاعل or فاعلة.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r12.anchor: وأما الطائف فيجوز أن يكون بمعنى: الطيف، مثل العافية والعاقبة، ونحو ذلك مما جاء المصدر فيه على فاعل وفاعلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r13.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r13.claim: Al-Aʿsha's line speaks of a visitation by a jinn, illustrating طائف.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r13.anchor: قال الأعشى (¬3): وتصبح (¬4) من غب السرى وكأنما (¬5) ... ألم بها من طائف الجن أولق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r14.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r14.claim: Al-Farra says طائف and طيف are equivalent: a likeness of an apparition or something that touches a person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r14.anchor: قال الفراء (¬6) في هذه الآية: (الطائف والطيف سواء، وهو ما كان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r15.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r15.claim: Al-Layth defines Satan's طائف or طيف as the whispering that envelops a person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r15.anchor: وقال الليث: (طائف الشيطان، وطيف الشيطان ما يغشى الإنسان من وساوسه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r16.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r16.claim: Some distinguish طيف as a passing thought and طائف as a thought; they say the former pattern is more common for verbal nouns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r16.anchor: ومنهم من قال: (الطيف كالخطرة، والطائف كالخاطرة (¬2). وهذا أكثر لأن المصدر على فعل أكثر منه على فاعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r17.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r17.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r17.claim: Abu Amr says a طائف circles something, here Satan's whisper, while طيف is the touch or whisper itself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r17.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو (¬4): (الطائف ما يطوف حول الشيء، وهو هاهنا ما طاف به من وسوسة الشيطان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r18.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r18.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r18.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ataa's narration, explains it as an occurrence of Satanic whispering.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p547#2/r18.anchor: فأما التفسير، فقال ابن عباس في # رواية عطاء: (إذا مسهم عارض من وسوسة الشيطان)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r1.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas glosses the satanic touch as a provocation from Satan.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r2.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r2.claim: Mujahid and Said ibn Jubayr explain it as a man overcome by anger who remembers God and restrains his anger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد (¬4) وسعيد بن جبير (¬5): (هو الرجل يغضب الغضبة فيذكر الله فيكظم الغيظ)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r3.claim: In a report through Layth, Mujahid says it is a man about to sin who remembers God and desists.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r3.anchor: وروى ليث (¬6) عن مجاهد قال: (هو الرجل يهم بالذنب فيذكر الله فيدعه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi gives a similar explanation of the satanic touch.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r4.anchor: ونحو ذلك قال الكلبي (¬1)، وروى الحكم (¬2) عن عكرمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r5.speaker: ابن عباس من رواية عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ikrima's report through al-Hakam, identifies the tayf as anger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r5.anchor: وروى الحكم (¬2) عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية قال: (الطيف الغضب)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r6.claim: The اهل المعاني advise recalling God's anger at transgressors when feeling excessive anger, to avoid ruinous action.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r6.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (ينبغي للعاقل إذا أحس من نفسه إفراطا في الغضب أن يذكر غضب الله على المسرفين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r7.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r7.claim: Ataa reports from Ibn Abbas that they seek God's protection and then perceive God's greatness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r7.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد: استعاذوا فأبصروا عظمة الله تعالى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r8.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says they repent when they slip.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r9.claim: They recognize the satanic suggestion as sin, see it clearly, and recoil in fear of God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (يقول: إن المتقي إذا أصابه نزغ من الشيطان تذكر (¬7) وعرف أنها معصية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r10.claim: On this explanation, those who see discern where they have erred through remembrance and reflection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r10.anchor: فعلى هذا معنى (¬9) {مبصرون} أي: يبصرون مواقع خطاياهم بالتذكر والتفكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r11.claim: Abu Ishaq says they reflect on God's clear proof and thereby attain insight.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r11.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (أي: تفكروا فيما أوضح الله لهم من الحجة فإذا هم على بصيرة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r12.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r12.claim: Al-Farra glosses مبصرون as stopping once they see.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p552/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء: ({فإذا هم مبصرون} أي: منتهون إذا أبصروا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r1.claim: Here إذا is suddenative, as in the example خرجت فإذا زيد.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فإذا هم}. معنى (إذا) هاهنا: المفاجأة، كقولك: خرجت فإذا زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r2.claim: إذا in إذا مسهم functions like a conditional in having a response, but differs from إن because it denotes a time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r2.anchor: و (إذا) في قوله {إذا مسهم} (¬3) بمنزلة الجزاء في أن لها جوابا كجوابه، والفرق (¬4) بينها وبين الجزاء أن (إذا) عبارة عن الوقت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r3.speaker: الشافعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i illustrates the distinction legally: divorce conditioned with إذا takes effect at once, while the corresponding إن condition does not take effect unless he divorces her.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p554/r3.anchor: ولهذا قال الشافعي: (إذا قال لامرأته: إذا لم أطلقك فأنت طالق (¬7)؛ طلقت في الوقت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:198-201/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:198-201/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:198-201/r7.claim: Those mindful of God here are believers.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:198-201/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:198-201/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:198-201/r8.claim: When a satanic whisper touches them, they seek refuge, recognize their errors, and withdraw from disobeying God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:198-201/r8.anchor: { إذا مسهم } أصابهم { طيف من الشيطان } عارض من وسوسته { تذكروا } استعاذوا بالله { فإذا هم مبصرون } مواقع خطئهم، فينزعون من مخالفة الله.

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r4.claim: When a trace of Satan touches the God-fearing, they remember refuge in God, recognize the error and satanic trick, and guard themselves.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r4.anchor: hemen gözlerini açarlar hata noktasını ve Şeytan’ın hilesini görür, ihtiraz ederler

ELMALILI:7:200-205/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r5.claim: Although addressed to the Messenger, the passage also gives a general address to all believers.
ELMALILI:7:200-205/r5.anchor: Bu âyet, Resûlullah’a olan bu hitâbâtın bütün mü’minlere hitâb-ı âm olduğuna bir tenbîhi ihtivâ eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r1.claim: After the preceding command to be forgiving, if provocation tempts the Prophet or any believer to anger and retaliation, they should recognize Satan’s prompting, seek refuge in God, and remain patient and tolerant.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r1.anchor: cahillerin kötülüklerine kötülükle karşılık vermesine yol açacak bir kışkırtma duygusuna kapılırsa, bunun şeytandan gelen bir fitleme olduğunu bilerek şeytana kapılmaktan Allah’a sığınması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r2.claim: When destructive thoughts arise, the God-fearing activate their faculties, recall divine guidance about proper conduct, discern the truth, and act accordingly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r2.anchor: Allah’ın böyle durumlar karşısında nasıl davranmak gerektiğine dair uyarılarını, irşadlarını hatırlayarak basîretli yaklaşımlarıyla gerçeği, doğru ve isabetli tutumun ne olduğunu görüp ona göre hareket ettikleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r3.claim: The Quran calls piety the highest honor and value; one condition of it is not answering evil with evil or stooping to the ignorant, but choosing ease, generosity, peace, and reconciliation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:200/r3.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in “en yüksek şeref ve değer” kabul ettiği (Hucurât 49/13) takvâ erdemine sahip olmanın şartlarından biri de kötülüğe kötülükle cevap vermemek

BURHAN:v4p68/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p68/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p68/r2.claim: Insight is an enduring quality of the God-fearing that Satan may veil; remembering restores their sight. The form مبصرون conveys return to an existing quality, whereas يبصرون would suggest a newly acquired action.
BURHAN:v4p68/r2.anchor: لأن البصر صفة لازمة للمتقي وعين الشيطان ربما حجبت فاذا تذكر راى المذكور

ITQAN:v2p312/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p312/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p312/r1.claim: The word ṭāʾif means a passing visitation or whisper (lemma).

ITQAN:v2p390#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p390#3/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
ITQAN:v2p390#3/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says the Quran contains words from fifty languages, including many Arab tribal dialects and Persian, Roman, Nabataean, Abyssinian, Berber, Syriac, Hebrew, and Coptic.
ITQAN:v2p390#3/r1.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الواسطي في كتابه الإرشاد في القراءات العشر في القرآن من اللغات خمسون لغة

ITQAN:v2p390#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p390#3/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الواسطي
ITQAN:v2p390#3/r3.claim: Al-Wasiti gives ṭāʾif min al-shayṭān the dialectal meaning a sting in Thaqif.
ITQAN:v2p390#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ طائف من الشيطان ﴾ نخسة بلغة ثقيف

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r7.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports that Jabir heard the Prophet recite the word طائف with a long alif.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r7.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرء { إذا مسهم طائف } بالألف

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r8.speaker: أبو بصير
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r8.claim: Abu Basir reports from Abu Abdillah that the verse describes a servant who considers sin, remembers, and then refrains; al-Ayyashi transmits parallel versions through Abu Basir, Ali ibn Abi Hamza, and Zayd ibn Abi Usama.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r8.anchor: في الكافي بإسناده عن أبي بصير، عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألته

THALABI:v4p319/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r4.speaker: النخعي وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والأعمش وابن يزيد والجحدري وطلحة
THALABI:v4p319/r4.claim: These readers pronounce طيف; the remaining readers pronounce طائف. Both are Arabic variants, like الميت and المائت, with the same general sense.
THALABI:v4p319/r4.anchor: قرأ النخعي وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والأعمش وابن يزيد والجحدري وطلحة: طيف، وقرأ الباقون: طائف

THALABI:v4p319/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v4p319/r5.claim: Abu Amr distinguishes طائف as something circling an object and طيف as a touch, whisper, or passing thought.
THALABI:v4p319/r5.anchor: فقال أبو عمرو: الطائف ما يطوف حول الشيء والطيف اللمة والوسوسة الخطرة

THALABI:v4p319/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r6.speaker: بعض المكيين
THALABI:v4p319/r6.claim: Some Meccans distinguish a satanic whisper that circles a person from طيف meaning flesh or touch; طيف may also be a lightened form like هين and لين.
THALABI:v4p319/r6.anchor: وقال بعض [المكيين] : الطائف ما طاف به من وسوسة الشيطان والطيف اللحم والمس

THALABI:v4p319/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v4p319/r7.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr's doubled reading طيف supports treating it as an established form.
THALABI:v4p319/r7.anchor: يدل عليه قراءة سعيد بن جبير: طيف بالتثقيل

THALABI:v4p319/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p319/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the visitation as satanic incitement.
THALABI:v4p319/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان أي نزغ من الشيطان

THALABI:v4p319/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r9.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p319/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the satanic visitation to mean a sin.

THALABI:v4p319/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r10.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p319/r10.claim: Mujahid takes the satanic visitation to mean anger.

THALABI:v4p319/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p319/r11.claim: They remember, reflect, and recognize; Abu Rawq says they supplicate earnestly.
THALABI:v4p319/r11.anchor: تذكروا وتفكروا وعرفوا، وقال أبو روق: ابتهلوا

THALABI:v4p319/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
THALABI:v4p319/r12.claim: A reading attributed to Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr has فأملوا in place of تذكروا.
THALABI:v4p319/r12.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله بن الزبير: إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان [فأملوا]

THALABI:v4p319/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v4p319/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says an angry person remembers God and restrains his anger.
THALABI:v4p319/r13.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: هو الرجل يغضب الغضبة فيذكر الله فيكظم الغيظ،

THALABI:v4p319/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r14.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p319/r14.claim: Mujahid says a person intending a sin remembers God and abandons it.
THALABI:v4p319/r14.anchor: ليث عن مجاهد: هو الرجل هم بالذنب فيذكر الله فيدعه

THALABI:v4p319/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r15.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p319/r15.claim: Al-Suddi says the pious repent when they slip.
THALABI:v4p319/r15.anchor: وقال السدي: معناه إذا زلوا تابوا

THALABI:v4p319/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p319/r16.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v4p319/r16.claim: Muqatil says the believer recognizes a satanic prompting as disobedience, sees the mistake by reflection, and stops short of it.
THALABI:v4p319/r16.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إن المتقي إذا أصابه نزغ من الشيطان تذكر وعرف أنها معصية فأبصرها

NAHHAS:v2p169/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p169/r16.claim: The pious avoid sins; when Satan touches them, they reflect on God’s power and favors, leave the sin, and regain clear sight.
NAHHAS:v2p169/r16.anchor: والمعنى إن الذين اتقوا المعاصي إذا لحقهم شيء من الشيطان

NAHHAS:v2p169/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r17.speaker: أهل البصرة وأهل مكة
NAHHAS:v2p169/r17.claim: Basrans and Meccans use ṭaʾif; Medina and Kufa read ṭāʾif, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr is reported to read ṭayf with doubled yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v2p169/r17.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل البصرة وأهل مكة وقرأ أهل المدينة وأهل الكوفة

NAHHAS:v2p169/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r18.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v2p169/r18.claim: The normal Arabic form is ṭayf without a doubled yāʾ, from ṭāfa yaṭīfu; al-Kisai calls it shortened, meaning a thought in the heart or a dream image like ṭāʾif.
NAHHAS:v2p169/r18.anchor: كلام العرب في مثل هذا طيف بالتخفيف على أنه مصدر

NAHHAS:v2p169/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r19.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v2p169/r19.claim: Abu Hatim says al-Asmaʿi denied verbal nouns on the fīʿl pattern; Abu Jaʿfar answers that this is not a verbal noun but can mean ṭāʾif.
NAHHAS:v2p169/r19.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم سألت الأصمعي عن طيف فقال ليس في المصادر

NAHHAS:v2p169/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p169/r20.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v2p169/r20.claim: Mujahid is reported to read tadhakkarū with a doubled dhāl, which Abu Jaʿfar says has no grammatical basis.
NAHHAS:v2p169/r20.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد ( تذكروا ) بتشديد الذال ولا وجه له في العربية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r4.claim: When the pious remember, they regain their inherent sight; the verb yubsirun would instead suggest newly acquired seeing rather than return of a quality.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r4.anchor: لأن البصر صفة لازمة للمتقي، وعين الشيطان ربما حجبت فإذا تذكر رأى المذكور ولو قيل: (يبصرون) لأنبأ عن تجدد واكتساب

IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r9.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r9.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r9.claim: These readers read طيف without alif; Nafi, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Hamza retain alif and hamza.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p299/r9.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائى / طيف / بغير ألف وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r1.claim: One explanation takes the opening reference to the God-fearing generally, concerning everything one should avoid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r1.anchor: واتقوا قيل: عامة في كل ما يتقى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r2.claim: Another explanation restricts the reference to avoiding idolatry and sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r2.anchor: وقيل: الشرك والمعاصي، وقيل: عقاب الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r3.claim: A third explanation takes it as avoiding God's punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r3.anchor: وقيل: الشرك والمعاصي، وقيل: عقاب الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r4.speaker: النحويان وابن كثير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r4.claim: The two grammarians and Ibn Kathīr read ṭayf, without the alif.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r5.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r5.claim: The other seven readers read ṭāʾif, the active participle of ṭāfa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r5.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة طائف اسم فاعل من طاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r6.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr reads ṭayyif with a doubled yāʾ, on the fayʿil pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن جبير طيف بالتشديد وهو فيعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r7.claim: Ṭayf may be a verbal noun of ṭāfa yaṭīfu, or a shortened form comparable to mayyit/mayt or layyin/layn, since the verb has both yaṭīfu and yaṭūfu forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r7.anchor: فاحتمل أن يكون مصدرا من طاف يطيف طيفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r8.speaker: الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r8.claim: Al-Fārisī prefers taking ṭayf as a verbal noun and analogizes ṭayf to khāṭira and ṭāʾif to khāṭir.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r8.anchor: وإلى أن الطيف مصدر مال الفارسي جعل الطيف كالخطرة والطائف كالخاطر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r9.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī defines ṭayf as a touch or affliction and ṭāʾif as what circles around a person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r9.anchor: وقال الكسائي: الطيف اللمم والطائف ما طاف حول الإنسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya questions al-Kisāʾī's distinction by citing al-Aʿshā's comparison to a visitation of jinn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وكيف هذا؟ وقد قال الأعشى: وتصبح عن غب السرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r11.claim: Abū Ḥayyān answers that the line is consistent: a jinn's affliction may circle a person, or the simile describes a camel's speed and vigor as if seized by madness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r11.anchor: ولا يتعجب من تفسير الكسائي الطائف بأنه ما طاف حول الإنسان بهذا البيت لأنه يصح فيه معنى ما قاله الكسائي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r12.speaker: أبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r12.claim: Abū Zayd gives ṭāfa/yaṭūfu as coming and going, aṭāfa as circling people and approaching from all sides, and ṭāfa al-khayāl as a dream visitor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r12.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: طاف أقبل وأدبر يطوف طوفا وطوافا وأطاف استدار القوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r13.speaker: السهيلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r13.claim: Al-Suhaylī argues there is no active participle of a dream's visitation, since imagination is not real; he distinguishes the actual visitor in the verse about a punishment from God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r13.anchor: وزعم السهيلي أنه لم يقل اسم فاعل من طاف الخيال قال: لأنه تخيل لا حقيقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān cites the phrase about a visitor from God in 68:19 as an instance where ṭāʾif is a genuine active participle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r14.anchor: وأما فطاف عليها طائف من ربك فلا يقال فيه طيف لأنه اسم فاعل حقيقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r15.speaker: حسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r15.claim: Ḥassān's line about a jinniya whose ṭayf kept him awake uses ṭayf for a dream visitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r15.anchor: وقال حسان: جنية أرقني طيفها ... تذهب صبحا وترى في المنام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the two forms have the same sense, al-nazʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هما بمعنى النزع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r17.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r17.claim: Al-Suddī distinguishes ṭayf as madness from ṭāʾif as anger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r17.anchor: وقال السدي: الطيف الجنون، والطائف الغضب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r18.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r18.claim: Abū ʿAmr says both forms mean satanic whispering.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r18.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: هما بمعنى الوسوسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r19.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r19.claim: Other explanations equate them with a touch or dream vision; another assigns imagination to ṭayf and Satan to ṭāʾif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r19.anchor: وقيل: هما بمعنى اللمم والخيال، وقيل: الطيف النخيل، والطائف الشيطان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r20.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r20.claim: Mujāhid takes ṭayf as anger and explains that madness, anger, and whispering are called ṭayf because each is a touch from Satan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r20.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الطيف الغضب ويسمى الجنون والغضب والوسوسة طيفا لأنه لمة من الشيطان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r21.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r21.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr and al-Suddī say that when the God-fearing slip, they repent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r21.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن الزبير والسدي: إذا زلوا تابوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r22.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r22.claim: Mujāhid says that when they contemplate a sin, they remember God and abandon it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r22.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إذا هموا بذنب ذكروا الله فتركوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r23.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r23.claim: Ibn Jubayr says that when they become angry, they restrain their anger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r23.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: إذا غضب كظم غيظه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r24.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r24.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r24.claim: Muqātil says that when Satan touches them, they remember, recognize the act as sin, and stop out of fear of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r24.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إذا أصابه نزغ تذكر وعرف أنها معصية نزع عنها مخافة الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r25.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r25.speaker: أبو روق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r25.claim: Abū Rawq says they earnestly supplicate.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r26.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r26.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r26.claim: Ibn Baḥr says they seek refuge through remembrance of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p258/r26.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: عاذوا بذكر الله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r12.claim: The inward gloss takes piety here as avoiding associationism.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r13.claim: A satanic touch is the attribution of an act to someone other than God; remembering oneness restores the vision that God is the only agent.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156/r13.anchor: لمة منه بنسبة الفعل إلى غيره سبحانه وتعالى
